changelog: [Core Principles]: Added an explicit statement that because measured quality sits far above the floor, the default action at any completed clause-final connective/ender is to split; withholding a split now requires a concrete, nameable piece of information that would be lost, not generic caution about disfluency, density, or list structure — this pushes latency gain up without adding any new prohibition.

[Decision Procedure]: Reworded steps 5-6 so that only a specific, nameable loss of information (a word, referent, tense, or polarity that cannot be recovered) blocks a split; vague unease about a sentence being 'dense', 'disfluent', or part of a 'list/chain' no longer counts as sufficient grounds to withhold a <SEG> — this narrows how conservatively the existing checklist is applied, directly increasing segmentation frequency as the critic's 'segment more aggressively' direction requires, without touching [When to Segment] or [Never Segment], which were changed (and reverted) in the immediately preceding iteration.
